overall_summary: Bitcoin is steadying near 76k after a heavy long wipeout while spot ETF outflows and firm labor data keep near-term pressure on. Geopolitical de-escalation bets and upcoming peace talks offer some offset, but today’s NFP report remains the key unresolved catalyst. Overall tone is cautious and event-driven rather than clearly directional.
key_points: Strong jobs data may delay rate cuts
Oil drops and Ukraine peace talks eyed
NFP report today is main macro swing factor

items.title: BTC steadies near $76k after $1B+ long wipeout
items.summary: Bitcoin bounced from about $75,200 back toward $76,000 after Thursday's AI and tech stock rout slammed risk assets. Nasdaq dropped 5.5 percent on fears Democratic control could slow AI data-center spending, and that spilled straight into crypto. More than a billion dollars in leveraged positions got liquidated, overwhelmingly longs. Traders should care because leverage has been flushed, open interest is rebuilding, and the U.S. jobs report lands later today as the next macro catalyst while price sits on key support.
items.impact: Short-term volatility around support; flushed longs can fuel bounce if jobs data cooperates

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $430 million in one day
items.summary: U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $430 million in net outflows on Thursday, reversing the prior session's modest inflow. Fidelity's FBTC led with roughly $200 million out, followed by BlackRock's IBIT at $105 million. That extends a stretch of redemptions and brings recent multi-day outflows well over a billion. Traders should watch this because sustained ETF selling removes a key institutional bid and can amplify downside when risk appetite is already weak.
items.impact: Removes institutional demand and adds near-term selling pressure on BTC

items.title: Core Scientific exits Bitcoin mining by year-end
items.summary: Core Scientific told investors it will fully wind down Bitcoin mining by the end of 2026 and enter 2027 as a pure-play AI and high-density colocation provider. Mining already shrank to a small slice of revenue while AI hosting jumped past $215 million in the quarter. Other public miners are making similar pivots. This matters because it accelerates hashrate concentration among remaining low-cost operators and underscores how AI power demand is competing directly with mining for electricity and infrastructure.
items.impact: Structural shift in mining sector; potential hashrate consolidation longer term

items.title: Trump Media moves $342M BTC to Crypto.com
items.summary: Wallets linked to Trump Media transferred about 4,259 bitcoin, roughly $342 million, to a Crypto.com address in two batches. The coins came from addresses labeled as collateral for convertible notes, just weeks before a November 30 window when noteholders can demand cash repayment. Past similar moves were described as custody rather than sales, but the size and timing raise fresh selling concerns. Traders should monitor it because any actual distribution could add supply overhang into an already fragile market.
items.impact: Potential supply overhang and headline risk if coins are sold

items.title: $2.7B Bitcoin options expire with max pain $79k
items.summary: Roughly $2.6 to $2.7 billion in Bitcoin options expired this morning on Deribit, heavily skewed to calls with max pain near $79,000. Price was already trading well below that after the selloff, creating a potential gamma and positioning reset. The expiry sat just hours before the U.S. jobs report, leaving a short window without those hedges. This is relevant because large expiries often reduce volatility afterward or force dealers to adjust hedges, which can amplify the next directional move.
items.impact: Positioning reset that can cut short-term vol or amplify the post-jobs move

items.title: Greece sets 10% crypto gains tax, 15% on DeFi
items.summary: Greek parliament approved the country's first comprehensive crypto tax rules: 10 percent on individual capital gains above a 500-euro annual exemption, plus 15 percent on staking, lending and DeFi income treated as interest. Rules take effect in 2027 with a 12-month window to declare past gains without late penalties. Crypto-to-crypto swaps appear largely exempt. It is a European regulatory development rather than a U.S. catalyst, but it adds to the global tax net and could influence how other jurisdictions treat DeFi yields.
items.impact: Limited direct BTC price effect; incremental regulatory clarity and tax drag in Europe

items.title: October NFP Jobs Report Drops Today
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the October Employment Situation at 8:30 AM Eastern, the biggest macro catalyst of the day. Consensus looks for about 65,000 nonfarm payrolls after September's soft 29,000 print, unemployment steady at 4.2 percent, and average hourly earnings up 0.3 percent. Traders should care because a hot number keeps December Fed hike odds elevated near 70 percent and supports the dollar, while a miss could ease yields and lift risk assets including bitcoin.
items.impact: High volatility for USD, yields, and crypto risk appetite pending the print

items.title: Jobless Claims Hit 57-Year Low at 189k
items.summary: Initial unemployment claims fell 6,000 to 189,000 last week, matching the lowest level since 1969 and beating the 196-197k forecast. Continuing claims ticked up slightly to 1.718 million. This signals employers are still reluctant to lay people off even as hiring stays muted, keeping the labor market tight ahead of the full jobs report and giving the Fed cover to stay vigilant on inflation.
items.impact: Supports higher-for-longer rates narrative, firmer dollar and pressure on risk assets

items.title: Q3 Productivity Surges 3.6 Percent, Labor Costs Fall
items.summary: Nonfarm productivity jumped at a 3.6 percent annualized rate in the third quarter, well above the 2.8 percent expectation and up from a revised 2.1 percent prior. Unit labor costs dropped 0.7 percent, the first decline since early 2025. Stronger output per worker without rising wage pressure is disinflationary and helps corporate margins, but it also shows the economy can grow without overheating the labor market the Fed watches closely.
items.impact: Mixed: eases wage-inflation fears yet keeps growth solid for potential further tightening

items.title: ADP Private Payrolls Beat with 86k October Gain
items.summary: The ADP report showed private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, matching the prior month and beating the 67,000 consensus. Services led the gains while professional and business services continued to shed jobs. This private-sector snapshot pointed to resilient hiring just ahead of the official government payrolls number and kept markets focused on whether the labor market is cooling enough for the Fed.
items.impact: Reinforces solid labor backdrop that could sustain Fed hike bets and USD strength

items.title: ISM Services PMI Eases to 54.5, Prices Stay Hot
items.summary: The ISM Services index slipped to 54.5 in October from 54.9, still firmly in expansion for a 28th month but cooler than expected. New orders and business activity slowed while employment improved to 51.4. The prices-paid component stayed elevated at 73.0, underscoring sticky inflation in the dominant services sector that the Fed cannot ignore.
items.impact: Sticky services inflation keeps December rate-hike probability supported

items.title: Dollar Steady, Yields Dip Ahead of Payrolls
items.summary: The dollar index held around 101.55 to 101.80 as equity weakness drove some safe-haven flows into the yen while Treasury yields eased, with the 10-year near 4.84 percent. Fed funds futures still price roughly a 70 percent chance of a 25-basis-point hike in December. Markets are in wait-and-see mode for the jobs data that will set the tone for rates, the dollar, and risk assets into the weekend.
items.impact: Range-bound USD and yields until NFP resolves the near-term Fed path

items.title: Democrats Sweep US Midterms; Vance Blames Iran War
items.summary: Democrats seized control of both the House and Senate in a historic blue wave, delivering a sharp rebuke to President Trump. Vice President JD Vance bluntly said the Iran war caused the losses due to soaring gas prices, and Trump largely agreed while defending the campaign. Markets see gridlock and pressure for de-escalation as reducing escalation risk, with oil already plunging on the news. Traders should care because lower energy prices and political constraints on further military action typically support risk assets including crypto.
items.impact: Risk-on bid as oil falls and war-ending hopes rise

items.title: Iran Reports Multiple Tankers Hit by Mines in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran’s IRGC and army claimed five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire after striking naval mines on unauthorized routes through the Strait of Hormuz. UK maritime authorities separately reported a tanker hit by unidentified projectiles near Qatar. These incidents keep the critical oil chokepoint disrupted even as midterm results fuel de-escalation hopes. Crypto and risk traders watch this closely because any sustained Hormuz squeeze can reignite oil spikes, inflation fears, and risk-off moves.
items.impact: Sustains oil-supply risk and volatility premium

items.title: Oil Plunges Below $100 on Midterm De-escalation Bets
items.summary: Brent crude tumbled to multi-week lows below one hundred dollars a barrel, with WTI dropping under ninety, after the Democratic sweep and Vance’s Iran-war comments. Traders are pricing higher odds that Trump will seek a diplomatic off-ramp rather than fresh strikes. Falling energy costs ease inflation pressure that has weighed on rates and risk assets. For a crypto trader this is a clear potential tailwind if the oil decline holds.
items.impact: Eases inflation and supports risk appetite

items.title: US-Russia-Ukraine Peace Talks Set for Abu Dhabi Nov 10-11
items.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will mediate working-level trilateral talks with Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi next week focused on security guarantees, de-escalation and ending the war. Zelenskyy met the envoys in Brussels and confirmed the schedule after earlier Putin contacts. Progress here would reduce a major geopolitical overhang. Markets and crypto often rally on credible peace signals that lower global uncertainty.
items.impact: Potential reduction in Europe war risk premium

items.title: US Sanctions Indian and Turkish Networks Aiding Iran
items.summary: The Treasury hit an India-based maritime fraud network accused of issuing fake flags for Iran’s shadow oil fleet plus a Turkish firm servicing sanctioned Iranian airlines. The moves form part of Operation Economic Outcast aimed at choking Tehran’s war funding. Fresh secondary sanctions raise compliance costs and geopolitical friction with key trading partners. Traders note this keeps economic warfare elevated even if kinetic action slows.
items.impact: Maintains sanctions pressure without new kinetic escalation

items.title: Russian Strike Death Toll Hits 42 at Ukrainian Aid Center
items.summary: Ukrainian police said the toll from Monday’s Russian bombing of an aid distribution site in Zaporizhzhia’s Komyshuvakha village has risen to forty-two dead with dozens still missing under rubble. Russia continued overnight strikes on logistics targets. The attack underscores ongoing intensity ahead of next week’s peace talks. Persistent battlefield escalation can cap risk appetite until diplomacy shows real progress.
items.impact: Keeps Ukraine war risk elevated short-term
